nodes.summary: A real number $x$ is dyadic when $x = a / 2^n$ for some integer $a$ and some natural number $n$, that is, when $x$ lies in $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$.
nodes.title: Dyadic rationals

nodes.summary: Let $\tau = (1 + \sqrt{5})/2$ be the golden ratio. A real number $x$ is a golden integer when $x = a + b\tau$ for some integers $a$ and $b$. Since $\tau^2 = \tau + 1$, these are exactly the elements of $\mathbb{Z}[\tau]$.
nodes.title: Golden integers

nodes.summary: Let $B$ and $S$ be sets of real numbers. A permutation $f$ of $\mathbb{R}$ is piecewise linear with breakpoints in $B$ and slopes in $S$ when $f(x) = x$ for every $x \notin [0, 1]$, and there are a natural number $n$ and points $0 = t_0 < t_1 < \dots < t_{n+1} = 1$, all in $B$, such that for each $i \le n$ there is $s \in S$ with $f(x) = f(t_i) + s (x - t_i)$ for all $x \in [t_i, t_{i+1}]$.
nodes.title: Piecewise-linear maps with prescribed breakpoints and slopes
